# --skip-platform leaves a platform out of the --platform=all matrix, and says
# so rather than passing it over in silence: the skip line is how a run reports
# what it did not cover.
#
# Distinct from a platform's own ProbeTest skip, which answers "this host
# cannot run it". android can run on a developer's machine -- that is exactly
# when it costs, a Gradle project built and run per fixture -- so nothing about
# the host says to leave it out and the caller does. `go tool verify` passes
# it unless -full, the same flag that puts android's Go tests behind -short.

sngl test --platform=all --skip-platform=none app.sngl
stdout '--- SKIP platform=none: left out by --skip-platform'
! stdout '=== platform=none'

# The rest of the matrix still runs: the flag names platforms, it does not
# narrow to one.
sngl test --platform=all --skip-platform=none app.sngl
stdout '=== platform=html'

# Naming none of them runs everything, which is what says the skip above was
# the flag and not the fixture.
sngl test --platform=all app.sngl
stdout '=== platform=none'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    ui.text(value="hi")
}

func testItRenders(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.assert(true)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    main
}
